/-!
# Erdős Problem 249

*Reference:* [erdosproblems.com/249](https://www.erdosproblems.com/249)
-/

open scoped Nat

namespace Erdos249

/--
Is
$$\sum_{n} \frac{\phi(n)}{2^n}$$
irrational? Here $\phi$ is the Euler totient function.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_249 : answer(sorry) ↔ Irrational (∑' n : ℕ, (φ n) / (2 ^ n)) := by
  sorry

end Erdos249

reformulations.difference: The Lean series is indexed by all natural numbers, including zero, rather than the conventional positive-integer indexing of the totient series.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Nat.totient 0 = 0, so the extra term is zero. Moreover, 0 ≤ φ(n)/2^n ≤ n/2^n and the majorant is summable, so tsum denotes the ordinary convergent real series. In /workspace/review/scratch.lean I proved summability, equality with ∑' n : ℕ, (φ(n+1) : ℝ)/2^(n+1), and the resulting irrationality equivalence, without sorry.
